title: Synthesis of biodiesel from Annona muricata – Calophyllum inophyllum oil blends using calcined waste wood ash as a heterogeneous base catalyst
author: Adepoju
materials: Analysis of the spent catalyst was studied after reusability and recyclability to depict its morphological characteristic by BET and the effect of reaction on the CaO by XRD. Observation showed that the SBET (Surface area) and the total pore volume increased as the reusability continued, while the basic site (BS), the total basic site (TBS), and the basic site density (BSD) of the spent catalyst decreased (Table 10). This is an indication that catalyst recyclability, purification, and reusability decreased the basic strength of the catalyst during the reaction process. The main aim of catalyst regeneration is targeted at restoring the high surface area and high dispersal of the element in the catalysts [26]. Furthermore, the effect of leaching within the reactor can easily lead to coverage of active surface sites hereby decreasing the biodiesel yield. The results displayed by XRD analysis alongside with the BET displayed that the percentage decrease to (25.43%) in CaO derived from CWWA was very high after reusability and regeneration. steps.title: Extract seed oils by Soxhlet
steps.instruction: Place the cleaned milled seed powder of Annona muricata and Calophyllum inophyllum in a Soxhlet extractor, add n‑hexane as solvent, and run the extraction at the boiling point temperature of n‑hexane for 70 min to obtain the oil; recycle the excess n‑hexane and reuse it, and keep the residual cake for animal feed.

steps.title: Determine oil physicochemical properties
steps.instruction: Measure the physicochemical properties of the extracted Annona muricata and Calophyllum inophyllum oils (e.g., density, viscosity, acid value, iodine value, etc.) to assess suitability for biodiesel synthesis.

steps.title: Prepare waste‑wood‑ash catalyst
steps.instruction: Treat the waste wood ash (WWA) obtained from the local bakery as follows: soak the ash in distilled water for 30 min, decant the floating particles, filter the suspension and discard the filtrate, oven‑dry the retained wet ash (PWWWA) at 110 °C until a constant weight is reached, then calcine the dried ash in a programmable muffle furnace at 1100 °C for 3 h; allow the calcined waste wood ash (CWWA) to cool to room temperature for 48 h before use.

substeps.instruction: Soak WWA in distilled water for 30 min.
Decant and remove floating particles.
Filter the suspension; discard filtrate.
Oven‑dry the filtered ash at 110 °C until constant weight.
Calcine the dried ash at 1100 °C for 3 h.
Cool the calcined ash to room temperature for 48 h.

steps.title: Characterize fresh catalyst
steps.instruction: Perform the following analyses on both CWWA and the original WWA:

substeps.instruction: Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) to examine surface topography.
Fourier‑Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy; record the wavenumber ranges and transmittance percentages:
• 1760.4 – 1077.27 cm⁻¹, transmittance 1.79 % – 9.14 % (C‑Cl, CO₃²⁻, N‑H wagging/twisting, O=C=O bending).
• 21148.0 – 1636.36 cm⁻¹, transmittance 9.14 % – 81.97 % (C‑C, C=C, C=N, C=O, CHO, C≡C, C≡N, O=C=O low‑energy, O‑H, O‑Ca‑O bending).
• 32928.0 – 3272.08 cm⁻¹, transmittance 3.29 % – 74.12 % (O‑H bending, O=O, N≡O).
X‑ray Diffraction (XRD) analysis to identify crystalline phases and quantify elemental composition.
BET nitrogen adsorption isotherm to obtain:
• Specific surface area (N₂‑AA) = 1.1 m² g⁻¹,
• Total pore volume (TPV) = 0.004 cm³ g⁻¹,
• Basic site concentration (BS) = 34 μmol g⁻¹,
• Total basic sites (TBS) = 71 μmol g⁻¹,
• Basic site density (BSD) = 62 μmol m⁻² (values as listed in Table 3).
Hammett indicator test to determine the basic strength of CWWA (values reported in Table 3).

steps.title: Analyze spent catalyst after reuse
steps.instruction: After catalyst reusability tests, characterize the spent CWWA using BET and XRD as follows (Table 10):

substeps.instruction: BET nitrogen adsorption:
• N₂‑AA = 1.4 m² g⁻¹,
• TPV = 0.008 cm³ g⁻¹,
• %CaO = 25.43 % (decrease from 62.83 % in fresh CWWA),
• BS = 86 μmol g⁻¹,
• TBS = 86 μmol g⁻¹,
• BSD = 61.43 μmol m⁻².
XRD analysis to confirm the reduction of CaO phase (from 62.83 % to 25.43 %).
Note the increase in surface area and total pore volume, and the decrease in basic sites and basic site density, indicating loss of basic strength during reuse.
